Your fan-out tier is the one I'd tune first. 20 distinct IPs in an hour on one key can be a single user on a phone moving between cell towers, or a key someone posted on a forum. Counting distinct countries and ASNs per key in that window separates the two: a mobile user stays on one carrier's network, a leaked key spreads across many.

It only needs to run after the suspicious tier trips, so it can be async and stay off the validate() path. A free offline ASN database covers the counting. If you also want to know whether those IPs are VPN exits or hosting ranges, IPGeolocation.io (IPGeolocation.io/documentation/ip-security-api.html) returns those flags (I work on it), though that part is on paid plans.
